stem.en: Why do spring tides come on both full moon days and new moon days?

text.en: The Moon is closest to the Earth on both days

feedback.en: No. The Moon's distance is not what makes these two days the same.

text.en: The Sun's heat is strongest on both days

feedback.en: No. The tide is a matter of pull, and heat does not raise it.

text.en: Sun, Earth and Moon lie in one straight line

feedback.en: Yes. In a line, the pulls of the Sun and the Moon combine.

text.en: The Moon is at its brightest on both days

feedback.en: No. The new moon does not shine in our sky at all.

explanation.en: On full moon and new moon days the Sun, the Earth and the Moon are in a straight line. The two pulls combine, so high tides are unusually high and low tides unusually low.

hints.en: Think of where the Moon stands in the two positions.
